BiblicalUsage: Garaz means to cut off, and it appears once, in Psalms 31:22, where the psalmist says in his haste, I am cut off from before thine eyes. He thought God had cut him off, yet the same verse says God heard the voice of his supplications when he cried.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the feeling of being cut off is the haste of fear, not the truth of God; the psalmist said it in haste, and God heard him anyway; I hold that even when I feel cut off, He hears my cry.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
